extraction_notes.note: The baseline-network description (text and equations) appears twice, in Section 2 and Section 5.1, and both copies of the hidden-layer equation carry \label{eqn:hidden}; the \eqref in Section 5.3 resolves to the Section 2 copy. Both equation pairs are kept as environment facts, but only the Section 5.1 prose is a definition node.
Section 7 (Improvements to the Neural Network Model) is a set of empty leftover subsections that reuse the labels subsec:soft-voting and subsec:PCA of Sections 5.2 and 5.3.
Feature and metric definitions are itemize lists whose items are sentence fragments; each list is one definition node rather than one node per introduced symbol.
Empirical observations read off the results table are emitted as claims with numerical rigor rather than remarks, since they are the paper's stated findings.
Benchmark profile (Table 1), model settings (Table 2) and results (Table 3) are tables of data; they carry no node and are reached only through the claims of Section 8.
Experimental set-up prose (train/validation/test split ratios, hardware, chosen hyperparameters, RF configuration, runtime) and the introduction's restatements of contributions were left out.

nodes.statement: Formally, the activation of the i-th neuron in the hidden layer is given by a_i^(1)=ReLUleft(sum_j=1^r w_ji^(1)x_j+b_i^(1)right),~i=1,2,dots,20, where r is the number of neurons of the input layer, x_j is the j-th feature (normalized, see Section~), and w_ji^(1) and b_i^(1) are weights and biases of the i-th neuron in the hidden layer, respectively. The activation of the output neuron is given by a^(2)=sigmaleft(sum_i=1^20 w_i^(2)a_i^(1)+b^(2)right),\\ where w_i^(2) and b^(2) are weights and the bias of the output neuron, respectively. In these two equations, ReLU(x)=x, & if x > 0,\\0, & otherwise,~sigma(x)=frac11+e^-x are ReLU and sigmoid functions, respectively.
